summary: npm package ships a Microsoft-login phishing HTML page as its only content
details: The package's sole shipped file is index.html (declared as main), which contains an obfuscated script impersonating a Cloudflare Turnstile challenge. After the CAPTCHA callback fires, the script reconstructs a URL from fragments including 'gin.micros' (Microsoft login lookalike) and calls window.location.replace() to redirect the browser. There are no lifecycle scripts and no JavaScript entrypoint, so npm install and require() of this package do nothing on the installer's machine — the phishing payload only executes when the HTML file is opened in a browser. This is registry abuse (using npm as hosting for phishing content) rather than a supply-chain attack against consumers who install the package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
